s: Upload code, get an autoscaling endpoint/event-handler with zero servers - billed per millisecond of use.
w: The provider runs your handler in ephemeral sandboxes scaled per concurrency. Events invoke it: HTTP via gateway, queue messages, schedules, object uploads. State must live outside (DB, cache) since instances vanish. Cold starts add latency after idle periods; provisioned concurrency mitigates for hot paths.
use: Spiky or unpredictable traffic (viral campaigns, nightly bursts)
Glue/integration work: webhook receivers, ETL steps, thumbnail triggers
Multi-region fan-out where per-region idle cost would be wasted VMs
MVPs validating ideas before committing to server fleets
avoid: Sub-millisecond latency paths (cold starts + gateway hops)
Long-running jobs beyond execution time limits (chunk or use workers)
Chatty fan-out calling relational DBs - connection storms exhaust pools

props.memory_mb: Bigger memory also allocates more CPU proportionally

size.rps_per_instance: ~200 rps per concurrent execution context (default assumption)

pat.d: Functions react to streams of facts; nothing polls anything.
Object upload triggers function -> transforms -> writes warehouse.

pits: Downstream connection storms at scale - use RDS Proxy / HTTP DBs / connection pooling
Cold-start SLO breaches - provision concurrency for p99-sensitive routes
Vendor limits (15min runtime, payload caps) discovered late - design chunking upfront
tips: Cost story: pay-per-use beats idle VMs below ~30-40% utilization; crossover favors containers above
Mention observability: distributed tracing becomes essential when logic scatters into functions
